Glorious, intense and utterly barmy. Delivers on so many levels. Fights as the Space Marine you always knew deep down they were REALLY like.

Highs (no spoilers):
The intro sequence. The finalé sequence. Most of the bits between start and end. The intro sequence (mentioned again for good measure). Chainsaws. Thunderhammers. Jump Packs. Jump Packs with a Thunderhammer. Thunderhammer Impacts. Kills. Gore. Sound effects. The effortless flow of combat. Kinetic impacts. Energy impacts. The setting. The story. The acting. Laying waste to the foes of Mankind on a frankly double-genocidal level.

Lows: The Titan bit was a little underwhelming for me when it finally happened (but I'd just read Ian Watson's "Space Marine" so was hoping for something way better).

Only 10 hours played, but F### M£ what a fun 10 hours. Worth every penny.
Maybe its a generic action adventures and linear story game, but the warhammer universe and story is still entertaining tho

In the grim darkness of the 41st millennium, there is only war.

This game is so good that almost ten years later, I still regularly come back to it and rate it in my top games of all time.

The campaign is great, good story and characters but it's made by the brutality of the combat. Before DOOM 2016 became the game it is, Space Marine pioneered 'push forward combat' mechanics by forcing you to regain health by spilling the blood of your foes. It's good fun, if a little short with some rather generic feeling level design, but it is serviceable and stands aside for the main event; slaughter in the Emperor's name. Your armour even becomes progressively gore soaked in SP, and its a shame that didn't carry over to any MP modes. The voice acting is particularly stellar, as is the case with most 40k games, with Captain Titus (Mark Strong) leading the show.

Where this game truly stands out is it's exterminatus mode. This is one of the most intense 4 player coop PVE modes out there. You fight massive waves of lunatic orks using majestic and suitably brutal imperial weapons, with other objectives thrown in like point capture and randomly generated challenges. You go through 4 maps/stages on each game. The mode is executed perfectly, with battles always getting epic and frenetic providing a challenge no matter how good you are. There's always more than enough enemies to go around.

What makes all of this so long lasting is the controls. They always do exactly what you tell them to, its snappy and fast, allowing you to switch between stabbing and punching your foes into oblivion, to unloading double barrel storm bolters at oncoming targets and back again instantly, allowing for much finer control of your combat rhythm than most games. This allows you to massacre the ridiculous hordes you face in exterminatus with precise efficiency, that is for once exactly what you would absolutely expect from a genetically modified super soldier raised for centuries of unending warfare against the nightmares from the void that wish to exterminate mankind.

I've added this specific paragraph ages after I wrote this review because I've realised yet another thing that makes this game feel so good. In the lore, even unarmed space marines are regarded as weapons, and the game is entirely consistent with this. Every single enemy in Exterminatus mode CAN be defeated in a hand to hand brawl, even the bigger boss type orks and Traitor marines. It takes skill and timing, but I've managed to do well in rounds using just my fists, shoulders and a combat knife, killing some of the biggest enemies by stunning them at the right moment and then laying into them in melee (with no melee weapon equipped). The game is designed in such a way that there is no reason for you to ever stop slaying, whether you're surrounded by a horde or hunting single targets, the brutality never lets up.

The weapons are all unique and savage, even the smallest firearm, the humble bolt pistol, can do better than its larger brethren if used well. And while on the topic of unique things, relic gave us full on customisation of our marines' armour patterns and colour schemes.


My only complaints are that there aren't more maps for exterminatus (there are 8 total) or more PVE modes that build on it. The other is that certain weapon upgrades are gated behind the PVP multiplayer, which isn't something I have much interest in. I will probably play this for many more years to come and pray that the Emperor delivers us a sequel. Hell I'd pay full price for a next gen remake that only updates the graphics and audio. Provided they don't try and make it cartoony and dumb like DOW3...
Looks great, interesting storyline and satisfying glory-killl animations.
